stop_conditions: 1. the payload swap breaks a landed assertion that would need weakening to pass

deviations.derivation: Section 1 stores the WINDOWLESS whole-sweep `SpineFrameSweep` on the canonical `Surface::SpineFrameSurface` variant, and Section 2 moves the per-profile-edge window data (s0/s1/v0/v1) OUT of the enum payload into derived views. The landed B-rep constructor (spine_sweep.rs:192-201) stores ONE per-face windowed realization per side face in that enum variant; once the payload is a windowless whole sweep, each side face can only carry the SAME whole-sweep support (full ring in v), so face.surface() reports the full-ring parametric domain. The landed modeling conformance volume test samples each face over its own try_range_tuple domain; measured empirically with the real formula: per-face windows give -0.9999999999999976 (abs 1.0, passes), while four whole-ring side faces give -2.999999999999993 (abs 3.0, FAILS the 1e-4 assertion against 1.0). The assertion would need weakening (volume tolerance ~2.0) to pass. The conformance file is NOT in this packet's write_allow, so it cannot be updated in place.

The packet itself classifies the two landed geometry test files as 'mechanical compilation fixes only; restore no assertion name, weaken no assertion'. surface_variant_forwarding_all_landed_methods asserts the enum-carried surface's range is (0,1) x (0,0.25), that `inverse()` swaps the v-window on the enum payload (inverse.v0() == 0.25), and that `parameter_range` forwards a stored per-face window. A windowless whole-sweep payload reports (spine domain) x [0,1] and has no per-face v0()/v1() window to swap; every one of those assertions changes value or disappears. That is a semantic rewrite, not a mechanical compilation fix, so the packet's own test-file rule forbids the windowless payload.

notes: BG-KV2-501-C6 stopped at stop condition 1 BEFORE implementation, on a design conflict between Section 1/2 and two immovable landed constraints. (1) The canonical Surface enum must stay Clone/Serialize/Deserialize (every truck topology S: Clone impl and the enum's own Transformed/composition paths require it), which forces the stored recipe's spine to the closed canonical Box<Curve> carrier; the constructive Spine enum (Ph | General(Box<dyn SpineCurve>)) is not Clone/Serialize, so 'SpineFrameRecipe<Spine, ProfileLaw, FrameLaw>' cannot be the stored payload as literally written (compiler-verified: Spine does not implement Clone). (2) The B-rep constructor's per-face windowed realizations are pinned by two un-writable-or-non-weakenable landed tests: the modeling volume conformance (convex_prism_volume_matches_analytic, outside write_allow) and the geometry enum-payload window assertions (updatable only mechanically). A windowless whole-sweep payload necessarily changes both. Resolution needs an owner decision: either (a) write_allow grows to include truck-modeling/tests/spine_sweep_conformance.rs plus permission to re-express the geometry window assertions (whole-sweep enum semantics, per-face windows derived from the face wire), or (b) the enum-carried SpineFrameSweep keeps the realized window domain as part of its closed value and Section 2's 'not stored IN the enum' is read as referring to the realization decorator (SpineFrameSurface generic decorator) no longer being the stored payload. The worker measured the volume evidence with the real conformance formula (scratch test, since removed): windowed total -0.9999..., whole-sweep-per-face total -3.0. Anchors were verified at dispatch (pre-state): A1 pub struct SpineFrameSurface count 1, A2 SpineFrameSurface(SpineFrameSurface<Box<Curve>>) count 1, A3 fn refuse(_error: ConstructError) count 1. The tree is left at the dispatch HEAD with an empty diff (only the dispatch files PACKET.md/CONTEXT.md untracked); no code was committed.
